page: Amazon Web Services c6gn.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by AWS Graviton processors. It features 64 dedicated physical cores on the arm64 architecture, utilizing the AWS Neoverse-N1 CPU model running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor and does not include local storage or GPU hardware.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 97017.01 and a high software compilation score in Geekbench. The instance also demonstrates high throughput for static web serving at 44.93 GB/sec and Redis SET operations at 72.72 million operations per second. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by lower scores in single-threaded gzip compression and Geekbench single-core tests. Memory bandwidth for cached small blocks is strong, but overall Passmark memory scores and uncached large-block read/write speeds fall into the average to weak categories.

With a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps, this instance is optimized for network-heavy workloads. The ARM-based architecture provides resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for multi-threaded applications, though the lack of local storage requires reliance on external EBS volumes. Tradeoffs include lower single-threaded execution speeds and poor performance in low-parameter LLM text generation. The hardware profile is suited for multi-threaded workloads, static web serving, software compilation, and high-throughput network applications.
